sanskrit: vayaṃ tu lobhān mohāc ca stambhaṃ mānaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ imām avasthām āpannā rājyaleśabubhukṣayā
english: But we, out of greed and delusion, clinging to arrogance and pride, have fallen into this plight from craving for a mere shred of kingship.

sanskrit: trailokyasyāpi rājyena nāsmān kaś cit praharṣayet bāndhavān nihatān dṛṣṭvā pṛthivyām āmiṣaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Not with the sovereignty of all three worlds could anyone gladden us, who have looked upon our kinsmen slain upon the earth—we who hungered after spoils.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pṛthivīhetor avadhyān pṛthivīsamān saṃparityajya jīvāmo hīnārthā hatabāndhavāḥ
english: For the sake of the earth we forsook men who ought never to have been killed, men equal to the earth itself, and now we live on, bereft of purpose, our kinsmen slain.

sanskrit: āmiṣe gṛdhyamānānām aśunāṃ naḥ śunām iva āmiṣaṃ caiva no naṣṭam āmiṣasya ca bhojinaḥ
english: We greedy for the flesh, like dogs—nay, not even dogs—both the flesh is lost to us, and lost too are those who would have eaten it.

sanskrit: na pṛthivyā sakalayā na suvarṇasya rāśibhiḥ na gavāśvena sarveṇa te tyājyā ya ime hatāḥ
english: Not for the whole earth, not for heaps of gold, not for all the cattle and horses, ought those to have been given up who now lie slain.

sanskrit: saṃyuktāḥ kāmamanyubhyāṃ krodhāmarṣasamanvitāḥ mṛtyuyānaṃ samāruhya gatā vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Yoked to desire and wrath, filled with anger and intolerance, they mounted the chariot of death and went to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: bahu kalyāṇam icchanta īhante pitaraḥ sutān tapasā brahmacaryeṇa vandanena titikṣayā
english: Wishing much good fortune, fathers strive for sons through austerity, through chastity, through worship, and through forbearance.

sanskrit: upavāsais tathejyābhir vratakautukamaṅgalaiḥ labhante mātaro garbhāṃs tān māsān daśa bibhrati
english: Through fasts and through offerings, through vows and auspicious rites, mothers conceive their children and bear them for ten months.

sanskrit: yadi svasti prajāyante jātā jīvanti vā yadi saṃbhāvitā jātabalās te dadyur yadi naḥ sukham iha cāmutra caiveti kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetukāḥ
english: "If only they be born in safety; if only, once born, they live; if only, grown strong and esteemed, they grant us happiness here and hereafter"—so the wretched ones hope, intent upon their fruit.

sanskrit: tāsām ayaṃ samārambho nivṛttaḥ kevalo 'phalaḥ yad āsāṃ nihatāḥ putrā yuvāno mṛṣṭakuṇḍalāḥ
english: For those mothers this whole endeavour has come to nothing, utterly fruitless, in that their sons—young men with polished earrings—have been slain.

sanskrit: abhuktvā pārthivān bhogān ṛṇāny anavadāya ca pitṛbhyo devatābhyaś ca gatā vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Without having tasted a king's enjoyments, without having discharged their debts to the ancestors and the gods, they have gone to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: yadaiṣām aṅga pitarau jātau kāmamayāv iva saṃjātabalarūpeṣu tadaiva nihatā nṛpāḥ
english: When, dear friend, the parents of these princes were as if made of love for them, in their very prime of strength and beauty those kings were struck down.

sanskrit: saṃyuktāḥ kāmamanyubhyāṃ krodhaharṣāsamañjasāḥ na te janmaphalaṃ kiṃ cid bhoktāro jātu karhi cit
english: Yoked to desire and wrath, unsteadied by anger and elation, never at any time will they taste the least fruit of their birth.

sanskrit: pāñcālānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca hatā eva hi ye 'hatāḥ te vayaṃ tv adhamāṃl lokān prapadyema svakarmabhiḥ
english: Of the Pāñcālas and the Kurus, even those who are unslain are as good as slain; while we, by our own deeds, must come to the lowest worlds.

sanskrit: vayam evāsya lokasya vināśe kāraṇaṃ smṛtāḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putreṇa nikṛtyā pratyapatsmahi
english: We ourselves are accounted the cause of the destruction of this world; through the treachery of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son we were brought to this pass.

sanskrit: sadaiva nikṛtiprajño dveṣṭā māyopajīvanaḥ mithyāvṛttaḥ sa satatam asmāsv anapakāriṣu
english: Ever skilled in deceit, a hater, living by guile, he behaved falsely toward us at all times, though we had done him no wrong.

sanskrit: aṃśakāmā vayaṃ te ca na cāsmābhir na tair jitam na tair bhukteyam avanir na nāryo gītavāditam
english: We desired our share, and so did they; yet neither did we win, nor did they: by them this earth was not enjoyed, nor its women, nor its song and music.

sanskrit: nāmātyasamitau kathyaṃ na ca śrutavatāṃ śrutam na ratnāni parārdhyāni na bhūr na draviṇāgamaḥ
english: Neither counsel in the assembly of ministers, nor the learning of the learned, nor jewels beyond price, nor land, nor any gaining of wealth.

sanskrit: ṛddhim asmāsu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vivarṇo hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya nṛpateḥ saubalena niveditaḥ
english: Seeing that prosperity of ours, he grew pale, sallow, and gaunt; and so he was reported by the son of Subala to King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: taṃ pitā putragṛddhitvād anumene 'naye sthitam anavekṣyaiva pitaraṃ gāṅgeyaṃ viduraṃ tathā asaṃśayaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro yathaivāhaṃ tathā gataḥ
english: His father, out of fondness for his son, consented to him though he stood in unrighteousness, without ever heeding the patriarch, the son of Gaṅgā, or Vidura. Without a doubt Dhṛtarāṣṭra has come to the same pass as I.

sanskrit: aniyamyāśuciṃ lubdhaṃ putraṃ kāmavaśānugam patito yaśaso dīptād ghātayitvā sahodarān
english: By failing to restrain his impure, greedy son, who followed the bidding of his lusts, he has fallen from his blazing fame, and has caused brothers to slay one another.

sanskrit: imau vṛddhau ca śokāgnau prakṣipya sa suyodhanaḥ asmatpradveṣasaṃyuktaḥ pāpabuddhiḥ sadaiva hi
english: And that Suyodhana, ever bent on hatred of us, ever evil-minded, has cast these two aged ones into the fire of grief.

sanskrit: ko hi bandhuḥ kulīnaḥ saṃs tathā brūyāt suhṛjjane yathāsāv uktavān kṣudro yuyutsur vṛṣṇisaṃnidhau
english: What kinsman of noble birth would speak to those who wish him well as that base man, eager for war, spoke in the presence of the Vṛṣṇis?

sanskrit: ātmano hi vayaṃ doṣād vinaṣṭāḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ pradahanto diśaḥ sarvās tejasā bhāskarā iva
english: For through our own fault we are ruined for endless years, we who once burned across all the quarters with our splendour, like suns.

sanskrit: so 'smākaṃ vairapuruṣo durmantripragrahaṃ gataḥ duryodhanakṛte hy etat kulaṃ no vinipātitam avadhyānāṃ vadhaṃ kṛtvā loke prāptāḥ sma vācyatām
english: That man of enmity toward us came under the sway of evil counsellors; for Duryodhana's sake this whole lineage of ours has been brought down. Having slain those who should never have been slain, we have earned the world's reproach.

sanskrit: kulasyāsyāntakaraṇaṃ durmatiṃ pāpakāriṇam rājā rāṣṭreśvaraṃ kṛtvā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'dya śocati
english: Having made that wicked-minded, evil-doing destroyer of this lineage the lord of the realm, King Dhṛtarāṣṭra now grieves.

sanskrit: hatāḥ śūrāḥ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ viṣayaḥ svo vināśitaḥ hatvā no vigato manyuḥ śoko māṃ rundhayaty ayam
english: The heroes are slain, the sin is done, our own domain laid waste; having killed, our wrath has departed, and this grief now hems me in.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjaya kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ kalyāṇenopahanyate tyāgavāṃś ca punaḥ pāpaṃ nālaṃ kartum iti śrutiḥ
english: Dhanaṃjaya, sin once committed is undone by righteous deeds; and the man given to renunciation, the scripture says, has no power to commit sin again.

sanskrit: tyāgavāñ janmamaraṇe nāpnotīti śrutir yadā prāptavartmā kṛtamatir brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: Since the scripture holds that the man of renunciation incurs neither birth nor death, then, having found the path and settled his mind, he attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: sa dhanaṃjaya nirdvaṃdvo munir jñānasamanvitaḥ vanam āmantrya vaḥ sarvān gamiṣyāmi paraṃtapa
english: And so, Dhanaṃjaya, free of the pairs of opposites, a sage endowed with knowledge, I shall take leave of you all and go to the forest, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: na hi kṛtsnatamo dharmaḥ śakyaḥ prāptum iti śrutiḥ parigrahavatā tan me pratyakṣam arisūdana
english: For the scripture declares that the most perfect dharma cannot be attained by one who holds possessions; this, O slayer of foes, is plain to my own sight.

sanskrit: mayā nisṛṣṭaṃ pāpaṃ hi parigraham abhīpsatā janmakṣayanimittaṃ ca śakyaṃ prāptum iti śrutiḥ
english: By me, who craved possessions, sin was set loose; and the scripture says that what causes the ending of birth can indeed be attained.

sanskrit: sa parigraham utsṛjya kṛtsnaṃ rājyaṃ tathaiva ca gamiṣyāmi vinirmukto viśoko vijvaras tathā
english: So, casting off possessions and the whole kingdom as well, I shall go forth wholly released, freed of sorrow, freed of fever.

sanskrit: praśādhi tvam imām urvīṃ kṣemāṃ nihatakaṇṭakām na mamārtho 'sti rājyena na bhogair vā kurūttama
english: Do you rule this earth, made secure, its thorns cut away; I have no need of kingship nor of enjoyments, O foremost of the Kurus.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vyupāramat tataḥ pārthaḥ kanīyān pratyabhāṣata
english: Having spoken these words, the Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira fell silent; and then the younger son of Pṛthā made answer.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athārjuna uvācedam adhikṣipta ivākṣamī abhinītataraṃ vākyaṃ dṛḍhavādaparākramaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Arjuna spoke, as if stung past endurance, in measured and well-composed words, firm in argument and bold in speech.

sanskrit: darśayann aindrir ātmānam ugram ugraparākramaḥ smayamāno mahātejāḥ sṛkkiṇī saṃlihan muhuḥ
english: Showing himself fierce, the son of Indra, fierce in his prowess, that man of great splendour smiled and again and again licked the corners of his mouth.

sanskrit: aho duḥkham aho kṛcchram aho vaiklavyam uttamam yat kṛtvāmānuṣaṃ karma tyajethāḥ śriyam uttamām
english: Alas, what sorrow, what distress, what utmost faintness of heart, that after performing superhuman deeds you would forsake the highest fortune!

sanskrit: śatrūn hatvā mahīṃ labdhvā svadharmeṇopapāditām hatāmitraḥ kathaṃ sarvaṃ tyajethā buddhilāghavāt
english: Having slain your foes and won the earth, gained by your own proper duty, your enemies destroyed—how could you give it all up out of a lightness of mind?

sanskrit: klībasya hi kuto rājyaṃ dīrghasūtrasya vā punaḥ kimarthaṃ ca mahīpālān avadhīḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: For whence should kingship come to a coward, or again to a dawdler? And why then did you slay those guardians of the earth, blind with wrath?

sanskrit: yo hy ājijīviṣed bhaikṣyaṃ karmaṇā naiva kena cit samārambhān bubhūṣeta hatasvastir akiṃcanaḥ sarvalokeṣu vikhyāto na putrapaśusaṃhitaḥ
english: He who would choose to live by begging, attempting no undertaking by any work at all, stripped of well-being and owning nothing, becomes notorious in all the worlds, joined neither to sons nor to cattle.

sanskrit: kāpālīṃ nṛpa pāpiṣṭhāṃ vṛttim āsthāya jīvataḥ saṃtyajya rājyam ṛddhaṃ te loko 'yaṃ kiṃ vadiṣyati
english: O king, if you abandon your prosperous kingdom and take up the most wretched way of life of a skull-bearing mendicant, what will this world say of you?

sanskrit: sarvārambhān samutsṛjya hatasvastir akiṃcanaḥ kasmād āśaṃsase bhaikṣyaṃ cartuṃ prākṛtavat prabho
english: Renouncing all undertakings, stripped of well-being and owning nothing—why, my lord, do you long to go about begging like a common man?

sanskrit: asmin rājakule jāto jitvā kṛtsnāṃ vasuṃdharām dharmārthāv akhilau hitvā vanaṃ mauḍhyāt pratiṣṭhase
english: Born in this royal house, having conquered the whole earth, you would forsake dharma and artha entire and set out for the forest in your folly!

sanskrit: yadīmāni havīṃṣīha vimathiṣyanty asādhavaḥ bhavatā viprahīṇāni prāptaṃ tvām eva kilbiṣam
english: If the wicked should make havoc here of these oblations, abandoned by you, then upon you alone the sin will fall.

sanskrit: ākiṃcanyam anāśāsyam iti vai nahuṣo 'bravīt kṛtyā nṛśaṃsā hy adhane dhig astv adhanatām iha
english: "Possessing nothing is not to be wished for," thus did Nahuṣa declare; for in poverty deeds turn cruel. Fie upon poverty in this world!

sanskrit: aśvastanam ṛṣīṇāṃ hi vidyate veda tad bhavān yaṃ tv imaṃ dharmam ity āhur dhanād eṣa pravartate
english: The life of the seers that takes no thought for the morrow exists indeed—this you know; but that which men call dharma proceeds from wealth.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ saṃharate tasya dhanaṃ harati yasya yaḥ hriyamāṇe dhane rājan vayaṃ kasya kṣamemahi
english: Whoever steals a man's wealth steals his dharma along with it; and when our wealth is borne away, O king, to whom shall we show forbearance?

sanskrit: abhiśastavat prapaśyanti daridraṃ pārśvataḥ sthitam dāridryaṃ pātakaṃ loke kas tac chaṃsitum arhati
english: Men look upon the poor man standing at their side as though he were a condemned criminal; poverty is a grievous fault in the world—who could ever praise it?

sanskrit: patitaḥ śocyate rājan nirdhanaś cāpi śocyate viśeṣaṃ nādhigacchāmi patitasyādhanasya ca
english: The fallen man is pitied, O king, and the man without wealth is pitied too; I find no difference between the outcast and the destitute.

sanskrit: arthebhyo hi vivṛddhebhyaḥ saṃbhṛtebhyas tatas tataḥ kriyāḥ sarvāḥ pravartante parvatebhya ivāpagāḥ
english: From riches grown abundant, gathered from this source and that, all undertakings spring forth, as rivers spring from the mountains.

sanskrit: ardhād dharmaś ca kāmaś ca svargaś caiva narādhipa prāṇayātrā hi lokasya vinārthaṃ na prasidhyati
english: From wealth come dharma and pleasure and heaven too, O lord of men; for the very sustenance of life in the world is not secured without wealth.

sanskrit: arthena hi vihīnasya puruṣasyālpamedhasaḥ vyucchidyante kriyāḥ sarvā grīṣme kusarito yathā
english: For the man bereft of wealth and of little wit, all undertakings dry up, as the little streams in the summer's heat.

sanskrit: yasyārthās tasya mitrāṇi yasyārthās tasya bāndhavāḥ yasyārthāḥ sa pumāṃl loke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ
english: He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen; he who has wealth is a man in the world, and he who has wealth is also accounted learned.

sanskrit: adhanenārthakāmena nārthaḥ śakyo vivitsatā arthair arthā nibadhyante gajair iva mahāgajāḥ
english: By a poor man, however much he desires wealth and seeks to gain it, wealth cannot be won; wealth is bound fast by wealth, as great elephants are caught by elephants.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ kāmaś ca svargaś ca harṣaḥ krodhaḥ śrutaṃ damaḥ arthād etāni sarvāṇi pravartante narādhipa
english: Dharma and pleasure and heaven, joy, anger, learning, and self-control—all these proceed from wealth, O lord of men.

sanskrit: dhanāt kulaṃ prabhavati dhanād dharmaḥ pravartate nādhanasyāsty ayaṃ loko na paraḥ puruṣottama
english: From wealth lineage arises, from wealth dharma proceeds; for the man without wealth there is neither this world nor the next, O best of men.

sanskrit: nādhano dharmakṛtyāni yathāvad anutiṣṭhati dhanād dhi dharmaḥ sravati śailād girinadī yathā
english: The man without wealth cannot duly perform the works of dharma; for dharma flows forth from wealth as a mountain stream from the rock.

sanskrit: yaḥ kṛśāśvaḥ kṛśagavaḥ kṛśabhṛtyaḥ kṛśātithiḥ sa vai rājan kṛśo nāma na śarīrakṛśaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: He whose horses are lean, whose cattle are lean, whose servants and guests are lean—he, O king, is the truly lean man; not he who is lean of body.

sanskrit: avekṣasva yathānyāyaṃ paśya devāsuraṃ yathā rājan kim anyaj jñātīnāṃ vadhād ṛdhyanti devatāḥ
english: Reflect as is right; consider how it was between gods and asuras. O king, by what else than the slaughter of their kinsmen do the very gods prosper?

sanskrit: na ced dhartavyam anyasya kathaṃ tad dharmam ārabhet etāvān eva vedeṣu niścayaḥ kavibhiḥ kṛtaḥ
english: If another's property were not to be seized, how could one undertake that as dharma? This very conclusion has been fixed by the sages in the Vedas.

sanskrit: adhyetavyā trayī vidyā bhavitavyaṃ vipaścitā sarvathā dhanam āhāryaṃ yaṣṭavyaṃ cāpi yatnataḥ
english: The threefold knowledge is to be studied, and one must become wise; by every means wealth is to be acquired, and sacrifice performed with diligence.

sanskrit: drohād devair avāptāni divi sthānāni sarvaśaḥ iti devā vyavasitā vedavādāś ca śāśvatāḥ
english: By hostility the gods won their stations in heaven on every side—so the gods determined, and so run the eternal pronouncements of the Veda.

sanskrit: adhīyante tapasyanti yajante yājayanti ca kṛtsnaṃ tad eva ca śreyo yad apy ādadate 'nyataḥ
english: They study, they perform austerities, they sacrifice and make others sacrifice; and all that is the highest good—even what they take from another.

sanskrit: na paśyāmo 'napahṛtaṃ dhanaṃ kiṃ cit kva cid vayam evam eva hi rājāno jayanti pṛthivīm imām
english: Nowhere do we see any wealth that has not been taken by force from some other; and even thus do kings conquer this earth.

sanskrit: jitvā mamatvaṃ bruvate putrā iva pitur dhane rājarṣayo jitasvargā dharmo hy eṣāṃ nigadyate
english: Having conquered, they claim ownership, like sons over a father's wealth; the royal sages who have won heaven—theirs, it is declared, is dharma.

sanskrit: yathaiva pūrṇād udadheḥ syandanty āpo diśo daśa evaṃ rājakulād vittaṃ pṛthivīṃ pratitiṣṭhati
english: Just as the waters flow from the full ocean to the ten directions, even so does wealth go forth from the royal house and establish itself over the earth.

sanskrit: āsīd iyaṃ dilīpasya nṛgasya nahuṣasya ca ambarīṣasya māndhātuḥ pṛthivī sā tvayi sthitā
english: This earth was Dilīpa's, and Nṛga's, and Nahuṣa's, and Ambarīṣa's, and Māndhātṛ's; that same earth now rests in you.

sanskrit: sa tvāṃ dravyamayo yajñaḥ saṃprāptaḥ sarvadakṣiṇaḥ taṃ cen na yajase rājan prāptas tvaṃ devakilbiṣam
english: A sacrifice rich in goods, with all its sacrificial fees, has come to you; if you do not offer it, O king, you incur sin against the gods.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ rājāśvamedhena yajate dakṣiṇāvatā upetya tasyāvabhṛthaṃ pūtāḥ sarve bhavanti te
english: Those for whom a king offers the horse-sacrifice, attended with its fees—drawing near to its concluding ablution, they all become purified.

sanskrit: viśvarūpo mahādevaḥ sarvamedhe mahāmakhe juhāva sarvabhūtāni tathaivātmānam ātmanā
english: The great god of universal form, in the great rite of the all-sacrifice, offered up all beings, and himself as well, by his own self.

sanskrit: śāśvato 'yaṃ bhūtipatho nāsyāntam anuśuśruma mahān dāśarathaḥ panthā mā rājan kāpathaṃ gamaḥ
english: Eternal is this path of prosperity; we have never heard of its end. Great is the road that the son of Daśaratha trod: do not, O king, go by a crooked path.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca muhūrtaṃ tāvad ekāgro manaḥśrotre 'ntarātmani dhārayitvāpi te śrutvā rocatāṃ vacanaṃ mama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For but a moment, holding mind and hearing steady within your inmost self, listen; and then let my words find favour with you.

sanskrit: sārthagamyam ahaṃ mārgaṃ na jātu tvatkṛte punaḥ gaccheyaṃ tad gamiṣyāmi hitvā grāmyasukhāny uta
english: Never again, for your sake, would I tread the road travelled by the common throng; that road I shall now go, forsaking the pleasures of the village.

sanskrit: kṣemyaś caikākinā gamyaḥ panthāḥ ko 'stīti pṛccha mām atha vā necchasi praṣṭum apṛcchann api me śṛṇu
english: Ask of me, "What safe road is there to be walked alone?" Or, if you do not wish to ask, then hear me even unasked.

sanskrit: hitvā grāmyasukhācāraṃ tapyamāno mahat tapaḥ araṇye phalamūlāśī cariṣyāmi mṛgaiḥ saha
english: Forsaking the ways and comforts of the village, performing great austerity, eating fruits and roots, I shall wander in the forest among the deer.

sanskrit: juhvāno 'gniṃ yathākālam ubhau kālāv upaspṛśan kṛśaḥ parimitāhāraś carmacīrajaṭādharaḥ
english: Offering into the fire at its due season, touching water at both the twilights, lean, of measured fare, clad in deerskin and bark and wearing matted locks.

sanskrit: śītavātātapasahaḥ kṣutpipāsāśramakṣamaḥ tapasā vidhidṛṣṭena śarīram upaśoṣayan
english: Bearing cold and wind and heat, enduring hunger and thirst and weariness, drying up this body by austerity such as the ordinances prescribe.

sanskrit: manaḥkarṇasukhā nityaṃ śṛṇvann uccāvacā giraḥ muditānām araṇyeṣu vasatāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām
english: Ever hearing the cries, high and low, that delight the mind and ear, of the joyful beasts and birds that dwell in the woodlands.

sanskrit: ājighran peśalān gandhān phullānāṃ vṛkṣavīrudhām nānārūpān vane paśyan ramaṇīyān vanaukasaḥ
english: Breathing in the delicate fragrances of the blossoming trees and creepers, beholding in the forest the lovely woodland dwellers of every form.
